text: [See Lab.C. § 3600(a)] • Where these conditions exist, the employer is subject to liability for such injuries “in lieu of any other liability whatsoever” and “without regard to negligence.” [Lab.C. § 3600(a) (emphasis added)] a. [3:516] WCAB proceedings as exclusive remedy: Independent tort actions for work-related injuries are preempted. The WCAB proceedings provide the “sole and exclusive remedy” for physical and emotional injuries suffered in the course of employment. [See Lab.C. §§ 3602(a), 5300; and Shoemaker v. Myers (1990) 52 C3d 1, 18, 276 CR 303, 314] Cross-refer: Workers' Compensation Act preemption is discussed in detail at ¶ 15:505 ff. b. [3:517] Role of workers' compensation insurance: The standard form workers' compensation policy covers “compensation and benefits” due by an employer under the Workers' Compensation Act and gives the insurer the “right and duty” to defend the insured employer in proceedings before the WCAB. If the workers' compensation insurer accepts coverage of an injured worker's claim, the insurer substitutes for the employer and assumes the employer's liability for benefits owed to the employee under the Act.
